title: Policy-led deployment authorization and rollback controls
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers need a single, auditable control plane that enforces who can start/approve model rollouts (canaries, A/B tests, shadow traffic) and the conditions that automatically roll back unsafe deployments. Current behavior is ad-hoc: engineers rely on manual Slack approvals and inconsistent RBAC checks, causing audit gaps and delayed rollbacks. Goal: Ship a policy-first authorization layer that ties role-based approvals, time-bound delegations, and cryptographically logged sign-offs to rollout lifecycle events, and integrates with canary/A/B/shadow controls and auto-rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Authorization policies allow defining approval requirements per deployment channel (canary, A/B, shadow, full).
RBAC roles for deploy_requester, deploy_approver, and rollback_operator are supported and enforced via the control plane API.
Approval events are recorded in an append-only audit log with timestamp, approver id, decision, and signed token stored in KMS for tamper-evidence.
Console shows pending approvals with required sign-offs and a one-click approval flow; delegations can be granted with expiry.
Canary/A-B experiment specs can declare thresholds that, if crossed, trigger auto-rollback; these rules are enforced automatically in runtime.
Emergency bypass flow exists with escalation to on-call and explicit, recorded justification; bypasses are time-limited and visible in audit trails.
E2E tests cover happy path approvals, expired delegations, and auto-rollback triggers in staging and pre-prod environments.
proposal: Introduce a Policy Service that evaluates deployment requests against declarative rules. Policies are attached to projects and deployment targets and specify: required approvers (explicit list or role), minimum number of sign-offs, approval freshness window, and whether auto-rollback is allowed. Approvals issue short-lived signed tokens (JWT signed with a KMS-backed key). The serving control plane verifies tokens before progressing rollout stages. Canary controller will watch runtime metrics and consult the policy's rollback thresholds; on breach it initiates a rollback action and records the reason in the audit log. Console UX: pending approvals widget, granular permission management, delegation modal with expiry, and a policy editor with safe defaults. Integrations: Slack approvals via a secured webhook that returns signed tokens, and GitHub PR link correlation for traceability.
telemetry_requirements: Dashboard: approvals pending by project, avg approval latency, approvals by team.
Alert: approval latency > 24h for high-risk rollouts.
Metric: number of auto-rollbacks per release and top reasons (error-rate, latency, custom eval regression).
Trace: link rollout lifecycle events to request-level traces and canary metric timelines.
Audit export: ability to export signed approval events as NDJSON for compliance retention.
implementation_notes: Schema: add 'policy' and 'approval' tables to control plane DB (migrations required).
Auth: map existing SSO identities to RBAC roles; support SCIM group sync for enterprise customers.
Runtime: extend canary controller to accept policy-specified thresholds and to call rollback API when conditions met.
Console: new approval flows, delegation UI, policy editor; accessibility and keyboard flows required.
QA: staged rollout to internal team, then customer beta, with attack-surface review from Security.
Docs: PRD, runbook for manual rollback, and 'How approvals work' guide for customers.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Approval latency blocks business-critical launches. Mitigation: allow risk-tiered bypass with multi-step escalation and SLA for approvers.
Risk: Large number of approval records increases DB size. Mitigation: roll off older audit entries to cold storage with cryptographic hash anchors kept in primary DB.
Risk: Token replay or misuse. Mitigation: short token TTLs, per-deployment nonce, and KMS rotation with grace period.
Risk: Incorrect policy misconfiguration prevents deploys. Mitigation: dry-run mode and policy validation that warns on impossible-to-satisfy constraints.
